title: Fountains Abbey: virtual tour guide
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Medieval society, economy and culture
source: Written for history/y7 lesson 19 (Fountains Abbey virtual tour written guide (portal printable; site images from English Heritage and the National Trust))
intro: Lesson 19. A written guide for a virtual tour. Use the site's official online images and maps; work through the stops in order.

practical.aim: To find out what Fountains Abbey tells us about the Church in medieval England
equipment: A device with the site's official website or virtual tour
safety: Use only official sites (English Heritage, the National Trust)
method: Start with the site map: find the great church, the cloister, the cellarium and the mill
The great church and Huby's Tower: how big is it? What does that say about the monks' wealth?
The cellarium, about 90 m long: who lived and worked here, and what was stored?
The cloister and chapter house: where did the monks pray, read and meet?
The mill and the fields: how did the abbey make money from farming and wool?
The ruins: why is it ruined? (closed by Henry VIII in 1539)

questions.q: Who founded Fountains Abbey and when?

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box, answer: 'What does Fountains Abbey tell us about the Church in medieval England?' (one paragraph using the site).
questions.a: Wealth, farming, organisation and religious life, with site evidence

questions.q: Stretch: How useful is a ruined site compared with a written source?
questions.a: Shows size and layout well, but not people's thoughts; needs written records too

questions.q: Fountains Abbey became rich mainly from:
questions.a: A) Wool. Its large sheep flocks produced wool sold abroad.

questions.q: Big question: how did simple monks become so rich?
questions.a: Gifts of land, efficient sheep farming and the wool trade
